--- title: "Monte-Carlo Sampling Distributions of the Residual-Field Mean" jupyter: python3 --- ```{=html} ``` This report is **descriptive only**. It measures the sampling distribution of the residual-field domain mean under two designs — sampling that is uniform with respect to the analysis measure, and sampling by advected virtual floats — and displays those distributions. It constructs no test statistic, reports no $p$-value, and draws no conclusion about the assumptions D1a/D1b or the permutation test of `theory.tex`. Standard errors are given so the reader can judge what the Monte Carlo does and does not resolve. # The analysis domain Two analysis boxes sit inside the downloaded GLORYS region, both spanning $60^\circ$–$40^\circ$ W: **Box B** ($35$–$45^\circ$ N) straddles the North Atlantic Current and the Gulf Stream extension, and **Box A** ($22$–$34^\circ$ N) sits in the quiescent subtropical gyre. Temperature is downloaded over a common halo, from which the OHC truth and the fitted mean field are built; velocity is downloaded over a much larger region, because floats seeded near a box advect well outside it and return, and a float that leaves the velocity domain is lost from the experiment rather than merely lost from the box. ::: {#cell-fig-domain .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Analysis boxes inside the two downloaded GLORYS regions. Dashed: the velocity region driving advection, and the thetao region from which OHC truth and the mean field are built. Filled: the two analysis boxes. This report covers Box B only.](mean_estimation_mc_files/figure-html/fig-domain-output-1.png){#fig-domain width=846 height=726} ::: ::: This report analyses **Box B only**. Box A is drawn here because the same machinery is being run over it as a low-gradient contrast, reported separately. ::: {#cell-fig-days .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Residual field Z on single unaveraged days, in GJ per m2. Each day is the one whose P-weighted spatial standard deviation is nearest the 5th, 50th and 95th percentile of that box's 3,650 daily values, so the columns span typical low, median and high spatial variability. Rows carry their own colour scale, since the boxes differ several-fold in amplitude. Panel titles give the day and its spatial sd.](mean_estimation_mc_files/figure-html/fig-days-output-1.png){#fig-days width=119 height=790} ::: ::: @fig-days is the field the designs actually sample, shown unaveraged: each panel is one real day, selected by where its spatial dispersion $\mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z_k(\cdot,d))$ falls in the distribution of all $3{,}650$ days. Averaging over months would have smoothed away exactly the mesoscale structure that makes float position matter, so the quantiles are used to pick representative days rather than to build a composite. Three features carry through the whole report. First, the residual field is **strongly structured in space** at every quantile — even the 5th-percentile day carries a coherent front — and that structure is what makes *where* an array sits matter at all. Second, **daily spatial structure is almost the entire story**: Box B's median daily spread is $6.63$ GJ/m$^2$ against a total $\mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z) = 6.81$ that also includes variation of the domain mean across days and years, so the field's variability is overwhelmingly within-day spatial, not seasonal drift of the mean. Third, the two boxes differ sharply in amplitude — daily spread spans $5.4$–$8.7$ GJ/m$^2$ in Box B against $1.4$–$2.7$ in Box A. Both the bias and its Monte Carlo error scale with that amplitude, so the boxes are comparable only on a standardized $B/\sigma_k$ scale, never in raw GJ/m$^2$. # Estimand, truth, and estimator Let $\mathbb{P}$ be the normalized area $\times$ time probability measure on the Box B analysis domain: the base measure is surface measure restricted to the wet native GLORYS cells ($\mathrm{deptho} > 2000$ m, intersected with the data support), $A_j = e1t_j\,e2t_j$, tensored with counting measure on the $365$ days of the year and normalized. The target is the residual field's domain mean, $$\bar Z_k \;=\; \int_{\mathcal{X}} \tilde Z_k \, d\mathbb{P},$$ for each analysis year $k \in \{2010,\dots,2019\}$, where $\tilde Z_k$ is the year-$k$ OHC 0–2000 m field with the fitted mean field removed. A design is a finite point set $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^{n} \subset \mathcal{X}$; its estimator and bias are $$\hat Z^{(l,d)}_k \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \tilde Z_k\!\left(x_i^{(l,d)}\right), \qquad B^{(l,d)}_k \;=\; \hat Z^{(l,d)}_k - \bar Z_k .$$ $\tilde Z_k$ is a simple function on the native $1/12^\circ \times$ daily grid, so evaluation at $x_i$ is the cell-day lookup of the cell *containing* $x_i$ — not an interpolation. No partition coarser than the data grid is introduced anywhere, so there is no quadrature remainder to carry. ::: {#tbl-truth .cell execution_count=4} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

It is not: 2011 carries a residual $\bar Z_{2011} = -1.63$ GJ/m$^2$, or $0.25\,\sigma$, and the 2010–2014 years are fitted visibly worse than 2015–2019. This is leftover mean-field misfit, not a property of the sampling, and it **cancels from $B$ by construction** — $B$ differences a sample mean against the domain mean of the same field, so any spatially uniform offset $\delta_k$ in $\tilde Z_k$ drops out identically. It is carried in @tbl-truth rather than assumed away. # The two ensembles Both use the same $7{,}500$ designs' worth of sample sizes, so they differ only in *where* the points sit. **Advective.** Virtual floats deployed uniformly with respect to $\mathbb{P}$ over a $\pm 8^\circ$ seeding margin clipped to the velocity domain, advected through velocity year $l$, and retained only where they profile inside Box B. Ten velocity years $l \in \{2010,\dots,2019\}$ with $750$ independent deployment replicates each, paired with all ten analysis years: the pairing $l = k$ is **aligned** (flow and field are the same calendar year), all others **unaligned**. **The array is in renewal equilibrium, not ramping.** Floats are released from $540$ days before the analysis year on a schedule calibrated to hold the in-box standing stock flat — a non-negative deconvolution of the measured in-box response $g(u) = \mathbb{P}(\text{in box at age } u)$ against a constant target. The realized standing stock is $44$–$48$ floats across the year (mean $46$), so the day-of-year marginal is close to uniform by construction. This matters: an array ramping up from empty samples late in the year, and because the fitted mean field leaves a seasonal residual in the domain mean, that alone biases $\hat Z$ with no spatial concentration whatever. That artefact dominated an earlier version of this experiment; here it is removed by design rather than corrected afterwards. **Uniform (U-full).** For each advective design, $n$ iid draws with cell $\propto A_j$ and $\mathrm{doy} \sim \mathrm{Unif}\{0,\dots,364\}$ — a genuine iid sample from $\mathbb{P}$, matched to that design's own $n$. By construction $\mathbb{E}[B] = 0$, so this ensemble is simultaneously the reference distribution and an end-to-end check of the gather, the day-of-year indexing, and the $\bar Z_k$ subtraction. ::: {#tbl-nsize .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: : Retained sample size across the 7,500 advective designs. {#tbl-nsize} The spread in @tbl-nsize is much tighter than under a ramping array — a flat standing stock removes most of the between-design variation in $n$ — but it is not constant, and what remains is an outcome of the flow, since retentive years hold more floats inside the box. Two consequences to keep in view: $\hat Z$ is a ratio estimator (the denominator is random), and the two ensembles are matched *conditional on* $n$. # Uniform sampling: the reference distribution ::: {#cell-fig-ref .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Bias of the uniform-sampling estimator, B = Zhat - Zbar_k, one panel per analysis year. The ensemble is centred on the truth in every year: nine of ten deviations are under one Monte Carlo standard error, and the largest, 2017 at $-0.0055$ GJ/m$^2$, is $2.6$ se — about what ten such comparisons produce by chance, and $0.03\%$ of that year's $\sigma_k$. Note the resolution now available: the Monte Carlo standard error on a cell mean is $\approx 0.012$ GJ/m$^2$, against $\approx 0.05$ in the earlier ramping experiment. "Implied between-flow sd" is $\sqrt{\max(0,\,s^2 - \overline{\mathrm{se}}^2)}$, the part of the observed spread across the nine flows not accounted for by their own Monte Carlo error. {#tbl-aligned} Three features of @fig-heat and @tbl-aligned, stated as measurements: 1. **Column structure remains, but it is now a property of the field.** Column means run from $-0.114$ (2011) to $+0.069$ (2017) GJ/m$^2$. Every velocity year, including those five to nine years removed from the field in question, puts a similar bias on a given $\tilde Z_k$. In the earlier ramping experiment this column effect was almost entirely day-of-year coverage; with a flat standing stock it is not (see @tbl-decomp), and what remains is a flow-independent spatial effect — advected arrays under-sample the same parts of Box B whatever year's flow moves them. 2. **Every aligned cell sits below its own column mean.** The aligned entries are $-0.072$, $-0.148$, $-0.040$, $-0.158$, $-0.093$, $-0.105$, $-0.014$, $+0.045$, $-0.074$, $-0.063$ GJ/m$^2$; subtracting each column's mean over the ten velocity years leaves $-0.091$, $-0.034$, $-0.033$, $-0.060$, $-0.063$, $-0.072$, $-0.047$, $-0.024$, $-0.076$, $-0.090$. All ten are negative, with a mean of $-0.059$ GJ/m$^2$. Note that 2017's aligned bias is *positive* and still falls below its column: the contrast is not driven by the sign of the bias itself. 3. **Two noise scales are in play, and they now differ by a factor of two.** Replication over $750$ deployments per cell puts the deployment component of the error at $0.011$–$0.014$ GJ/m$^2$. The spread across the nine unaligned velocity years is $0.017$–$0.039$; removing each entry's own Monte Carlo error leaves a between-flow standard deviation of $0.014$–$0.038$, mean $0.024$ GJ/m$^2$. Unlike the earlier experiment — where these two scales coincided and the between-flow component came out at zero in two of five years — the flow year now demonstrably moves the unaligned cells, and the between-flow scale is the larger of the two. **Which scale applies to the diagonal.** Measured against Monte Carlo error alone, the ten contrasts are $-1.8$ to $-7.9$ standard errors. But that yardstick answers only "could this deployment ensemble have landed here by deployment randomness?", holding the flow fixed. The comparison being made is between one flow year and nine others, so the relevant scale is the between-flow spread, against which the same contrasts are $-1.0$ to $-3.7$. The second number is the honest per-year one. What the ten years add is a pattern no single year supplies: the contrast is negative in $10$ of $10$ years, and pooled across years it is $-0.059$ GJ/m$^2$ against a pooled standard error of $0.008$. Converting that to a $p$-value would require an exchangeability assumption over velocity years that this Monte Carlo cannot supply, and is deliberately not done here. ::: {#tbl-deff .cell execution_count=12} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ```{=html}

The design effect is $\sum_f \big(\sum_{i \in f} (\tilde Z_i - \hat Z)\big)^2 / \sum_i (\tilde Z_i - \hat Z)^2$, summing over floats $f$. {#tbl-deff} The advective histograms in @fig-grid are visibly wider than their uniform overlays. @tbl-deff attributes that: consecutive cycles of one float are near-replicates, so a design of $n$ profiles from $\sim 93$ floats carries roughly $n/1.9$ to $n/3.2$ independent observations, and the advective ensemble runs $1.4$–$1.8$ times wider than its $n$-matched uniform counterpart. The width gap is dependence, not bias. The design effect is larger here than under a ramping array because a spun-up float contributes a longer run of consecutive in-box cycles. # Temporal coverage versus spatial concentration Even with a flat standing stock, an advected array need not sample the year exactly uniformly, and the fitted mean field leaves a real seasonal residual: the spatial mean $\bar Z_k(d) = \int \tilde Z_k(\cdot, d)\, d\mathbb{P}_{\text{space}}$ varies over the year with a standard deviation of $0.4$–$0.7$ GJ/m$^2$. Any departure of the realized day-of-year marginal from uniform therefore biases $\hat Z$ without any spatial concentration whatever. Writing $\hat f^{(l,d)}$ for a design's empirical day-of-year distribution, the bias splits exactly in expectation as $$\mathbb{E}\big[B^{(l,d)}_k\big] \;=\; \underbrace{\sum_{d} \big(\hat f^{(l,d)}_d - \tfrac{1}{365}\big)\, \bar Z_k(d)}_{\text{temporal coverage}} \;+\; \underbrace{\Big(\mathbb{E}\big[B^{(l,d)}_k\big] - \sum_{d} \big(\hat f^{(l,d)}_d - \tfrac{1}{365}\big)\bar Z_k(d)\Big)}_{\text{spatial, given time}} .$$ The first term is what a design would suffer if it kept its own sampling days but drew its positions iid from $\mathbb{P}$ in space; it has the closed form above and is computed exactly, not simulated. The second is the remainder, attributable to *where* in the box the floats are on the days they sample. The split requires no assumption. ::: {#cell-fig-decomp .cell execution_count=13} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Total bias split into temporal-coverage and spatial-given-time components, per analysis year (panels) and velocity year (bars). Black dots are the total. ``` ::: ::: : Decomposition of the aligned cells, and the variability of the temporal term across the ten velocity years. {#tbl-decomp} Two measurements: - **The temporal term is now small.** Across the ten aligned cells it ranges $-0.066$ to $+0.076$ GJ/m$^2$, r.m.s. $0.036$ — against $0.159$ r.m.s. in the earlier ramping experiment. Holding the standing stock flat removed most, though not all, of the day-of-year artefact. - **The bias is therefore predominantly spatial.** The spatial-given-time component of the aligned cells runs $-0.172$ to $+0.060$ GJ/m$^2$ and carries the same sign as the total in all ten years. This is the substantive change from the earlier experiment, where day-of-year coverage accounted for $95\%$ of the 2016 aligned bias and $66\%$ of 2019; here the aligned bias is mostly about *where* the floats are, not *when* they sample. The temporal term also remains nearly constant down a column — its standard deviation across the ten velocity years is $0.0006$–$0.008$ GJ/m$^2$ — confirming that what day-of-year coverage survives is a property of the release schedule rather than of which year's flow pushes the floats. It follows that the column structure in @fig-heat is not a temporal artefact, and that the aligned-minus-column contrast of @tbl-aligned is essentially a contrast in spatial sampling. # Caveats - **One box.** Box B (35–45 N, 40–60 W) straddles the North Atlantic Current and Gulf Stream extension, the most strongly structured part of the domain (@fig-days). The low-gradient contrast, Box A, is being run separately; nothing here speaks to it. - **One flow realization per year.** The $750$ replicates per cell are independent *deployments*; the velocity field is a single realization of that calendar year. Every standard error quoted is over deployment randomness only, which is exactly why the between-flow scale, not the Monte Carlo se, is the right yardstick for the diagonal. - **No inference is drawn.** The aligned-minus-column contrast is reported as a measurement. Turning the ten negative signs into a $p$-value needs an exchangeability assumption over velocity years given the field, which this design cannot test; that is deferred. - **$n$ is endogenous.** Retention inside the box is an outcome of the flow, so $\hat Z$ is a ratio estimator, the sample sizes differ systematically by velocity year (@fig-nsize), and the two ensembles are matched conditional on $n$. Design-weighted and profile-weighted averages of the temporal component differ because $n$ and day-of-year coverage are correlated; the design-weighted average is the one consistent with $\mathbb{E}[B]$ and is used throughout. - **The spin-up ages the array.** Holding the standing stock flat requires releasing $\sim\!80\%$ of floats before the analysis year, which leaves the in-box age distribution older than a constant-rate array would give. The alternative — accepting the ramp — puts a far larger artefact into the day-of-year marginal, so this is the lesser distortion, but it is a distortion. - **$\tilde Z$ inherits the mean-field fit.** The seasonal residual driving the temporal term is itself what the trend-plus-harmonics basis failed to absorb; a different mean-field specification would move it. @tbl-truth reports the fit's leftover offset per year, which is largest in 2010–2014.
